etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English consumpcioun, from Old French consumpcion, from Latin cōnsūmptiō, from cōnsūmō +‎ -tiō, from con- (“with, together”) +‎ sūmō (“take; consume”). Equivalent to consume +‎ -tion.

definitions.definition: The act of eating, drinking or using.
The act of consuming or destroying.

quote.citation: 1963 February, “Diesel locomotive faults and their remedies”, in Modern Railways, page 99:
quote.text: Driving methods have a direct bearing on fuel consumption with every type of motive power.

definitions.definition: (pathology) The wasting away of the human body through disease.
(pathology, dated) Pulmonary tuberculosis and other diseases that cause wasting away, lung infection, etc.

quote.citation: 1763 June 20 (first performance), Samuel Foote, The Mayor of Garret. A Comedy, […], London:  […]  P[aul] Vaillant, […], published 1764, →OCLC, Act I, scene i, page 4:
quote.text: And then as to your ſcurvys, and gouts, rheumatiſms, conſumptions, coughs and catarrhs, tar-vvater and turpentine vvill make you as ſound as a roach.

definitions.definition: (euphemistic, dated)  Alcoholism as it precipitates a person's death (especially of natural causes).
